articles.title: Have any footballers ended their career with more own goals than goals? | The Knowledge
articles.summary: Plus: the earliest trophyless seasons, scoring off one’s backside (part II) and the origins of ‘shithousery’ Mail us with all of your questions and answers. “How many professional players have ended their senior careers with more own goals than goals for their own team?” wonders Peter Clark.
body: In the past we’ve looked at the players with the most own goals, but we haven’t looked at those who ended their professional career in debit. “Southampton cult hero Francis Benali scored only one ‘positive’ goal in his career and was legendary for banging in goal-of-the-month contenders at his own end, most notably a bullet header against Oldham in the 1993-94 season,” writes Daz Pearce. We could only find a couple of OGs for Benali, the other being against Manchester United in 1999-2000. But we were unable to find a comprehensive Southampton database, so there’s a chance we’ve missed some beauties.

Another unsentimental defender, Riccardo Ferri, the formidable stopper in Internazionale’s title-winning side of 1988-89, scored six goals and eight own goals in Serie A. He may be in credit overall – he scored three more goals in cup competitions, but we only have his OG data for Serie A. “ Jamie Carragher finished his career with four goals and seven own goals,” writes Dean Whearty. “He even managed to score two in one match against Manchester United in 1999!”

articles.title: Joining Shakhtar as they make base in London: ‘We’re here to show the world that we are alive’
articles.summary: With no ‘home’ games in Ukraine, Arda Turan’s side hit the road again, with Chelsea’s Stamford Bridge hosting their Champions League campaign. The morning has thinned out into low, wispy cloud. Beneath it, Shakhtar Donetsk’s players are going through their paces.
body: It masks the fact that, around dawn, air raid sirens disrupted the peace for everyone in view. Even here, in Shakhtar’s bucolic spa hotel base 15 minutes outside Lviv, nobody is safe from the threat of Russian rockets and drones. In Rivne, three hours’ drive to the north-east, another alarm had sent the players and staff down to the stadium’s shelter. The second half was delayed by 20 minutes and that, no matter the corner of the country or the vividness of the autumn colours, is a weekly reality.

So is a travel schedule any other Champions League club would recoil at. Shakhtar are about to hit the road yet again, because there remains no chance of playing European games in Ukraine. This season they will host matches in England for the first time, Stamford Bridge the winner in a beauty contest of three venues in the capital. If the border crossing into Poland is unforgiving, the journey could take anything up to 18 hours. The Guardian has been invited to join their trip to London for Wednesday’s game “at home” to AEK Athens.

articles.title: Lions to make history with France game in Cardiff
articles.summary: The British and Irish Lions are to take on France at Cardiff's Principality Stadium before their historic three-Test 2027 tour to New Zealand.
body: The British and Irish Lions women's team will play a historic first fixture against France at Cardiff's Principality Stadium before their 2027 tour to New Zealand.
Jo Yapp's side will face the French, ranked fourth in the world, in the Welsh capital on Friday, 27 August (19:30 BST).
The Lions face a Black Ferns XV the following weekend in Whangarei before the first of three Tests with New Zealand on 11 September.
"There are moments in sport that only come around once - and this is one of them," said head coach Yapp.

articles.title: Swimmer Archie Goodburn to meet prime minister over cancer funding
articles.summary: The Scottish athlete, who has inoperable brain tumours, previously made a tearful plea for more investment in brain cancer research on BBC Breakfast.
body: Swimmer Archie Goodburn is to meet the prime minister later after making a tearful plea for more investment to be put into brain cancer research.
The Scottish athlete, who was diagnosed with three inoperable brain tumours two years ago, said the Downing Street meeting offered a "unique opportunity for change".
He previously called for Andy Burnham to introduce a brain cancer lead to give patients a chance to "fight for their lives" during an appearance on BBC Breakfast.
Goodburn, 25, cried while looking down the camera, saying he was "on my knees begging" for help to ease the "unbearable suffering" of patients and their families.

articles.title: USWNT returnees earn 2-2 draw against Spain, an early World Cup wake-up call
articles.summary: The US were on the verge of losing two straight at home, but second-half goals from Ashley Sanchez and Mallory Swanson saved a draw. It was nearly time for the panic button. Maybe not to press it, but to look at it – to acknowledge that it’s within reach.
body: Then two players who had just returned to the team after long absences turned the tide. Ashley Sanchez and Mallory Swanson, after international scoring droughts of 1,648 days and 801 days, respectively, each scored in the second half to earn a 2-2 draw with the defending World Cup winners.

The result may have avoided the worst-case scenario, but the way it unfolded will give US fans pause. Just 255 days from the 2027 World Cup, the results raise fresh questions ahead of the side’s return to World Cup qualification in late November. But of course, there are caveats. Both teams were missing key players, with the World Cup still nine months away there’s plenty of time to course-correct.

Rather, the matches served as a helpful reminder to what many – including USWNT head coach Emma Hayes – already knew ahead of them: Spain, the top-ranked team in the world, are the first team in decades that can legitimately outclass the US women, who have long been the international standard bearers for the sport.
“They are world-class. We are still in progress,” Hayes said afterward. “I didn’t learn anything I didn’t already know.”

articles.title: How Ukrainians are uniting behind Shakhtar in London
articles.summary: Shakhtar Donetsk will be playing Champions League home games at Stamford Bridge this season. It is a scenario nobody wants ideally, but the UK's Ukrainian community is making the best of a difficult situation.
body: Artem Genne's favourite footballing memory is standing on the Donbas Arena pitch, waving the Champions League flag, before Shakhtar Donetsk faced Chelsea.
That was in 2012. Two years later, the Russian-backed capture of Donetsk led many Ukrainians to leave the city, including ardent Shakhtar supporter Genne.
A large number fled to other areas of Ukraine and beyond, with the region's football club forced to find a new home. Fourteen years later, they are still searching.
It has led Shakhtar to Kyiv, Lviv and Kharkiv in Ukraine, and Poland, Slovenia and Germany for European games.

articles.title: ‘Chip on his shoulder’: Brian Flores lawyers condemn racial stereotypes in NFL coaching report
articles.summary: Recruiting report prepared for Raiders’ 2024 search. Lawyers say assessment contains racial stereotypes. Flores sued NFL over discriminatory hiring in 2022. A recently unsealed recruiting report on Brian Flores contains multiple examples of “racial stereotypes” and amounts to unlawful retaliation…
body: The Korn Ferry report, made public on Tuesday and obtained by the Associated Press, lists six strengths and seven weaknesses that Flores’ attorneys say demonstrate the league’s continued reliance on racial stereotypes in hiring and its retaliation against the coach for his lawsuit alleging racial discrimination.

The report, first published by Front Office Sports, was prepared in connection with the Las Vegas Raiders’ head coaching vacancy in 2024. Flores is now the defensive coordinator for the Minnesota Vikings.

“The recently unsealed documents demonstrate two unfortunate, but unsurprising, realities,” attorney Michael J Willemin said in a statement. “First, that Mr Flores’ decision to hold the league and its teams accountable for systemic race discrimination has been met with unlawful retaliation. Second, discrimination continues to play a significant role in the hiring process for NFL Head Coaches, as evidenced by the fact that the candidate profile prepared for the Raiders leans heavily on racial stereotypes.”
Willemin added: “We and Mr Flores are committed to eradicating the institutional racism and retaliation that permeates the league, its teams and their partners.”

articles.title: 'Possessed' Davidson fills Weir gap as Scots set up glamour Sweden tie
articles.summary: Erin Cuthbert praises Lauren Davidson as Scotland overcome Caroline Weir's absence to set up a World Cup play-off tie with Sweden.
body: Scotland stalwart Erin Cuthbert says Lauren Davidson was "like a woman possessed" against the Czech Republic to help Melissa Andreatta's side overcome the absence of Caroline Weir and move closer to the 2027 World Cup.

The Brann forward scored the equaliser after the Czech Republic's shock early goal in Paisley as Scotland twice came from behind to set up a tie against heavyweights Sweden for a place in next summer's tournament in Brazil.

Scotland needed the industry and spark of the 25-year-old, because they reached the round two play-off without their two big names playing a huge part in the 3-2 win in the second leg for a 5-2 aggregate score.
Captain Weir pulled out after picking up an injury in the warm-up while Chelsea captain Cuthbert was introduced at half-time for just her second game of the season.

articles.title: NFL player Hill found liable for two counts of battery
articles.summary: A Miami jury has found Tyreek Hill liable for two counts of battery but not liable for the eight remaining claims made by Lakeeta Vaccaro, ending the high-profile civil trial involving the NFL wide receiver and his estranged wife.
body: Hill, who has played for the NFL's Kansas City Chiefs and Miami Dolphins, was found liable for two counts of battery - one stemming from an incident in January 2024, and another from April 2025.
The jury awarded Vaccaro $500,000 (£377,000) in compensatory damages but did not award her punitive damages.
The jury found Hill, 32, not liable for eight other counts that included battery, assault and continuing domestic violence.
The trial involved allegations of abuse made by Vaccaro, 30, who on the stand described instances in which Hill allegedly pulled her hair and "treated me like I was, just, a man."

articles.title: Iraola confirms desire for Champions League win and to avoid future trouble
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola Demands Liverpool Finish the Job Against LASK in Champions League Test. Liverpool have started their Champions League campaign properly, with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid at Anfield, but that only counts for so much if they follow it with a sloppy result in Austria.
body: The Liverpool head coach is not dressing it up. Away games in Europe are awkward, momentum disappears quickly and one careless night can leave a group-stage campaign looking far more complicated than it needs to be. Liverpool have three points already. Now they need to back that up.

Iraola said: “Champions League away games are always tough, we know this. It’s a team that in their competition, they won the competition. They are normally dominant, they spend a lot of time on the ball. And they have to change their approach a little bit when they go to face stronger opposition in the Champions League.
“We have this season the precedent of Celtic losing here 5-1 in extra-time. We have to respect them.

“Obviously we want to come here and win. I assume that probably we are the favourites but you have to come here, do the job and play well, because otherwise away games in the Champions League are never easy.”

articles.title: England Women's World Cup half-back dilemma
articles.summary: If there is one position that highlights the growth of the women's game in England, it is the competition for the half-back spot at the Rugby League World Cup.
body: Two Wigan stars provide one option, with Woman of Steel Jenna Foubister joined by her best friend and Warriors half-back partner Izzy Rowe. Then there's NRLW star and former Woman of Steel Georgia Roche, who has been tearing it up on the other side of the world.
It is a selection headache that England Women head coach Stuart Barrow welcomes as he prepares his side for three pool games, with a place in the semi-finals at stake.
They begin against Wales on October 17 before facing Australia and Samoa in what promises to be a tough pool-stage run.
In their opening contest, Barrow has opten to put the reigning Woman of Steel on the bench and start with Rowe and Roche in the halves.
